sections.heading: What is Builder pattern with progressive type safety?

blocks.text: **Builder pattern with progressive type safety** is a compile-time TypeScript concept that erases at emit — the run-time behavior is still JavaScript. Builder pattern with progressive type safety is where JavaScript dynamic typing surprises C# developers — implicit ToNumber, ToString, and truthiness rules that === and Object. This section defines terms before code — read the glossary, then run the snippets in Node or the browser console.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **Builder pattern with progressive type safety** beyond one-line definitions. Pitfalls for Builder pattern with progressive type safety
blocks.body: Treating Builder pattern with progressive type safety as pure syntax without compile-time or run-time behavior. Skipping validation at API/JSON boundaries. Ignoring strict compiler flags differences. Hand-waving in design review without a test or metric.

blocks.text: Prove mastery of **Builder pattern with progressive type safety** with a failing test that captures the edge case, a DevTools or heap snapshot showing the bug, and a clear tradeoff statement in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the compiler and emitted JS actually do — plus when the simple explicit version beats the clever abstraction.
